groups.name: The bank and the role
groups.why: How the bank makes money and where AI can help, the job itself, and the technology it names.

items.name: Bank Business Briefing
items.what: How the bank makes money, its corporate and commercial business in depth, and where AI work fits each revenue line.

items.name: Job Description
items.what: The Principal Applied AI Product Manager posting: what the role owns, what it requires and the tools it names.

items.name: Tech Stack Guide
items.what: Every technology named in the job: what it is, how the bank likely uses it, and what I need to know.

groups.name: How we deliver
groups.why: How every AI product goes from idea to adoption. Read the four pages in order: Product Workflow, Product Framework, Product Machine, Product Playbook.

items.name: Product Workflow
items.what: Start here. The six steps every AI product goes through, what happens in each, and the go/no-go gate at the end of each.

items.name: Product Framework
items.what: The rules every product follows: who decides at each gate, how success is measured, the quality bar, the AI principles and how each step is written up.

items.name: Product Machine
items.what: Who does each task in every step (Auto, Draft, Me or Partner), how tasks move toward automation (cut first, then automate), how the machine itself is measured, and how one product manager runs many projects at once.

items.name: Product Playbook
items.what: How to do each of the 44 sub-steps the first time and what to record, plus a short list of the 33 general agents. Their full specs are in the Agent Library.

groups.name: Relationship managers
groups.why: Relationship managers (RMs): the bankers who own business client relationships and win new business.

items.name: RM Executive Summary
items.what: Start here. The RM work on one page for the leaders of the RM business: the problem, the product, what RMs get first, the value, how fast and what I need.

items.name: The RM Assistant
items.what: The product: one AI assistant for each RM, its limits, its capabilities by moment in the RM's work and the core use case each answers.

items.name: RM Assistant Plan
items.what: How The RM Assistant gets delivered: the first 13 weeks as a chart, what could slow us down, who decides, how we prove the value and the risks.

items.name: RM Assistant Prototype
items.what: The RM Assistant as a clickable prototype: three agents (A1 in plain rules, A2 and A3 live on Claude) on sample data, the controls working, and a guided tour under 2 minutes.

items.name: RM Detail
items.what: Everything about the RM work in one document, for an AI to read: give it to an AI for the full picture. Built from the working files.

groups.name: Portfolio managers
groups.why: Portfolio managers (PMs): the bank's credit people paired with RMs (from its job postings), and the credit team around them.

items.name: PM Executive Summary
items.what: Start here. The portfolio manager work on one page for the leaders of the credit business: the problem, the product, what PMs get first, the value, how fast and what I need.

items.name: The PM Assistant
items.what: The product: one AI assistant for each PM, its limits, its capabilities by moment in the PM's work and the credit core use case each answers.

items.name: PM Assistant Plan
items.what: How The PM Assistant gets delivered: the first 13 weeks as a chart, what could slow us down, who decides, how we prove the value and the risks.

items.name: PM Assistant Prototype
items.what: The PM Assistant as a clickable prototype (version 5): the industry background draft, the borrower file, the review and memo drafts and an early warning preview, with at least three agents running live on Claude on sample borrowers, the controls working, and a voiced tour under 2 minutes.

items.name: PM Detail
items.what: Everything about the PM work in one document, for an AI to read: give it to an AI for the full picture. Built from the working files.

groups.name: Reference
groups.why: Pages to look things up in, in the order of the process: our words, the steps, the workflows, the agents and the controls. Kept in line with the plans by the audit.

items.name: Glossary
items.what: The words we use, one meaning each, the old wording we've retired, and the bank's terms still to map.

items.name: Steps Catalog
items.what: All 44 sub-steps of the Product Workflow, one card each: why it matters, what it produces and its tasks.

items.name: Workflow Maps
items.what: Each process drawn left to right, with its sub-processes branching off. Click any box for details.
items.source: memos/role-workflow.md, playbook/, product-machine.md, RM and PM memos Appendix B

items.name: Agent Library
items.what: Every agent in one place: what it does, what it may and may not do, and who's in charge. Filter by step or by who it serves.
items.source: playbook/agents.md, RM and PM memos Appendix A

items.name: Controls Catalog
items.what: All 25 controls, the safeguards built into each product, where each is set, built, proved and watched, and where each comes from (law, bank policy or our choice).

groups.name: Research
groups.why: Outside research we study and borrow from: where the value of AI is for each group we serve, and how to engineer a lean system.

items.name: Use Case Library
items.what: Where the value of AI is for each group of bankers we serve, and the outside research behind it: a section for relationship managers and one for portfolio managers.

items.name: Elon Mode
items.what: How Elon Musk engineers and improves systems: his five-rule algorithm, eight thinking habits, where the method went wrong, and the eight changes we made to our system.

groups.name: My workspace
groups.why: How I work: what's still open, the record of every audit, and how we write and keep our prompts.

items.name: Open Items
items.what: What is still open on the shared platform, the RM Assistant and the PM Assistant, and the decisions that cover both, with the questions for the bank on each track.

items.name: Audit Log
items.what: How we audit our work: the method, every check and when it runs, the record of every audit so far, and what to improve.

items.name: Prompting Guide
items.what: How we write prompts: Anthropic's advice in plain English, a fill-in template, three worked examples and a checklist.

items.name: Prompt Library
items.what: Our core prompts in one place, each with its version and what changed: the use case kit, a full product memo, the bank briefing, the showcase prototype, copying a user group's work to the next, and the full program audit.
